values.reason: The peak wavelength comes from the Wien displacement law fixed by the first star, and the photon energy is hc over it. A star's radius or luminosity would cancel, but neither is a node of the graph (no Stefan-Boltzmann relation is part of the problem), so a C built on it would be forced, not physical.

checks.name: feasibility: complete (R and D at three values in two phrasing pairs); infeasible strata recorded
phrasing pairs: same frame, numeral and unit; word counts within 3
D kinds: co-present and other event; D not on the target; rationale; scene clause

d_rationales: The outburst of the third star raises the temperature of that star only; it does not change the peak of the second star, so the answer for the second star is the stated one.
The outburst came after the spectrum had been recorded, an event after the stated process; the star radiated at its stated surface temperature when its spectrum was recorded.
values.scene_clause: A third star in the same field is observed with the same spectrometer. The second and the third star brighten from time to time in outbursts.
